name: Weather
description: Current conditions for one city, refreshed on a timer and kept readable when the network is gone
author: Lattice

config.label: City
config.help: A city name. The first match from Open-Meteo's geocoder is used.

config.label: Refresh every
config.help: Open-Meteo updates its current conditions every 15 minutes; asking more often returns the same numbers.

sections.title: Setting the city
items: Type a city into City in the inspector. The first match from Open-Meteo's geocoder wins, so be specific.
The widget never asks for your location — you type the place, and only that place is looked up.
No API key is involved: the service is free and open, which is the only reason this widget can be published.

sections.title: Units and refresh
items: Units switches between Celsius with km/h and Fahrenheit with mph. The request asks for them, nothing is converted here.
Refresh every defaults to 30 minutes, because Open-Meteo itself only updates current conditions every 15.
Asking more often than that returns the same numbers, so a shorter interval buys nothing.

sections.title: When the network is gone
items: The last reading stays on the card, with a line saying how long ago it was taken, instead of an empty box.
Readings are cached per city and per unit, so two cities never overwrite each other's numbers.
The age line refreshes every minute even when no new reading is due.

sections.title: What it can reach
items: Only two hosts are allowed: the geocoder and the forecast service. Nothing else is reachable from this widget.
If a host were missing from that list the card says so outright — that is an authoring mistake, not a flaky network.

sections.title: If it says no permission
items: The card needs the network and storage permissions: one to fetch, one to keep the last reading.
Grant them again and the next refresh picks up without a restart.

changes: First release: current conditions from Open-Meteo, with no API key.
The last reading is cached per city and unit, so a dropped network leaves readable numbers.
Celsius or Fahrenheit, refreshed between 15 and 180 minutes.
